user.description: Choose the meters you already have in Home Assistant. Meters from the Energy dashboard are filled in. Heat pump, batteries, consumers and appliances are set up afterwards via Configure.

bronnen.title: Meters and solar forecast
bronnen.description: The solar kWh counters are also used to compare, per quarter hour, how much sun was expected and how much came.

data.p1_power: Current grid power (P1 meter, + is import)
data.import_energy: Grid import (kWh counters, e.g. tariff 1 and 2)
data.use_energy_forecast: Use the solar forecast from the Energy dashboard
data.pv_forecast_sensors: Extra solar forecast from sensor attributes (optional)

net.title: Fast metering
net.description: Optional: the EMS reads the HomeWizard P1 meter directly every second, within your own network. Enter its IP address; the local API must be enabled in the HomeWizard app. Without an address the EMS follows the Home Assistant sensor (every 5 seconds), which is plenty for forecasting.

data.p1_host: IP address of the HomeWizard P1 meter (optional)

warmtepomp.title: Heat pump and weather
warmtepomp.description:
With its own kWh meter and an outdoor temperature sensor the EMS learns how much the heat pump uses at which temperature. The weather forecast then sets the expected heating use.

Also choose the signal that the heat pump is making hot water (for example 'Domestic hot water in progress'). The EMS then splits the use into heating and hot water: heating depends on temperature, hot water follows a daily pattern learned from the past weeks.

data.dhw_active: Heat pump is making hot water (binary sensor, optional)

accu.title: Battery
accu.description:
The EMS does not control the battery: set it to its own self-consumption (zero on the meter). The EMS only reads charge and power and calculates when it will be full and empty.

Virtual: the battery exists only in the calculation and follows the P1 meter like a real battery on self-consumption.

Zendure: read locally via the zenSDK; only the IP address is needed.

Via entities: any other battery, via the sensors of its own integration. The state of charge is required; power keeps the consumption model clean.

data.name: Name
data.host: Zendure: IP address of the battery
data.power_invert: Power sensor is inverted (+ is discharging)

verbruiker.title: Consumer with its own model
verbruiker.description:
For a consumer with its own kWh counter, such as a hot tub or charger. The EMS does not control it but learns its use per hour of day and per outdoor temperature and includes that in the forecast.

If it has a thermostat, also choose the set and measured temperature. The EMS then learns how much it uses when at temperature and when calling for heat, and adjusts the next hours accordingly.

apparaat.title: Appliance with programs
apparaat.description:
For a washer, dishwasher or dryer, for example via Home Connect. Choose the operation state: when a program runs or has a delayed start, the EMS schedules its use, up to the finish time if you also choose that sensor.

The EMS also learns from the past months how often and at what hour the appliance usually starts, separately for workdays and weekends, and includes that habit in the forecast. It keeps its own log for this, because the recorder only keeps 10 days.

Without its own kWh meter the EMS estimates the use per cycle from how much more the house uses while the appliance runs; until learned, the default below applies.

data.name: Name
data.state: Operation state (or a binary sensor that is on while it runs)
data.program: Active program (optional, kept in the log)

error.soc_required: Choose a state of charge sensor.
error.cannot_connect: The battery cannot be reached at this address via the local API.

options.entiteiten: Other battery, via entities of its integration
